title: SYSK Selects: How the Donner Party Worked
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the Stuff You Should Know episode on the Donner Party. Josh introduces it, then the hosts open with banter about the fake "Hu(f)Ju"/"Wofu" human-flesh tofu hoax and a note about an error on the HowStuffWorks article. They cover the Donner Party's background: George Donner as captain, James Reed's wagon, Lansford Hastings and the Hastings Cut-Off, the lost weeks in the Utah desert, the snowbound camps at Truckee Lake and Alder Creek in the Sierra Nevada, the Forlorn Hope snowshoe group and its cannibalism, the rescue parties, Lewis Keseberg's accusations, and the debate over whether cannibalism actually occurred. The episode ends with listener mail and the sign-off.

segments.title: Intro and tofu hoax banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the SYSK Selects episode on the Donner Party. Josh and Chuck chat about PBS American Experience and then about the fake Hu(f)Ju human-flesh tofu hoax, which fooled media outlets.

segments.title: Corrections and the Donner Party setup
segments.summary: The hosts say the HowStuffWorks article on the Donner Party has errors, such as the timeline and the party's name. They introduce George Donner as the wealthy farmer and James Reed as the financier whose double-decker wagon irritated others. The chuck wagon origin is discussed.

segments.title: Westward migration and Lansford Hastings
segments.summary: The hosts cover the push to populate California before the Gold Rush, with John Sutter at New Helvetia (Fort Sutter). Lansford Hastings promoted California and wrote a guidebook describing the Hastings Cut-Off as a shortcut.
topics: Immigrants Guide to Oregon and California

segments.title: Hastings Cut-Off and lost weeks
segments.summary: The Hastings Cut-Off was never tested by Hastings, who claimed it was easy. The party split, with part going on the Cut-Off. They failed to find Hastings at Fort Bridger, found his note, and took a southern route that cost weeks, lost wagons, and cattle, and killed some members in the desert.

segments.title: Stanton, Reed's fight, and snowbound camps
segments.summary: Charles Stanton returns with provisions and guides. James Reed kills Snyder in a fight and is banished. The group reaches the Sierra Nevada in November and camps at Truckee Lake and Alder Creek as snow piles up. A diary entry describes the snow and wagons being abandoned.

segments.title: Starvation and cannibalism at the camps
segments.summary: The snowbound camps run out of food. They eat their dogs, shoelaces, hides, blankets and bones, and kill their pack animals. The Forlorn Hope snowshoe party sets out and later begins cannibalism, starting with Antoine, then Jay Fosdick, while the guides are killed.

segments.title: Rescue parties and Keseberg
segments.summary: Survivors reach Fort Sutter and rescue parties are sent out. James Reed joins a relief effort, complicated by the Mexican-American War. Lewis Keseberg is found alone among the dead and is accused of murder and cannibalism. He later sues for defamation.

segments.title: Evidence debate and aftermath
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the lack of forensic evidence of human bones at the campsites and possible explanations. They recount the survivors who were reunited, the survival rates by group, and the effect on migration before the Gold Rush. Hastings' reputation was ruined.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener mail is read about a Back to the Future joke. The hosts mention the HowStuffWorks search for Hastings and close with contact info and credits.
